claims.text: The election is about good and evil in Costa Rica.
The country has always been a great example of strong modern views and stable stances in Central America.
This area has always been tolerant and that has helped the country in many ways.
The country needs to vote for good and vote away evil.

implicit_assumptions: The candidate referred to as 'the singer' represents an 'evil' position.
Election of that candidate will cause the economy to take a hit.
decomposition.reasoning_relation:
causal and normative (candidate
tick→negative outcomes → requires voting for good)
scope_notes: Applies to Costa Rica's presidential election.
uncertainty: Statements are presented with the modality 'I think' indicating tentative belief and lack of supporting evidence.

Inference.supporting_quote: If the singer is elected it is going to take a giant leap back.  The economy will also take a hit.
Inference.structure_objection: The author infers that because the seller’s election would cause economic harm, the only way to avoid it is to vote for good, but he provides no evidence that voting for the alternative actually prevents these harms or that the harms are solely due to the sing
Inference.alternative_interpretation: Even if the singer caused harm, a vote for good does not logically guarantee it is avoided – many other factors influence outcomes.
